description.p: Dusk Studio is a deliberately constrained, portastudio-style digital audio workstation. Fixed 24-channel topology with a fixed signal chain (HPF, 4-band EQ, FET/Opto compressor, sends, pan, mute/solo, fader), four aux buses, and a mastering chain with passive program EQ, bus compressor, tape saturation, and limiter.

Built for musicians who want to commit to sounds and finish songs instead of endlessly tweaking. Inspired by Tascam Portastudio hardware: every parameter is visible, no plugin chains, no bus reordering, no waveform-level editing.

Dusk Studio 0.17.0 puts Multi-Comp 2 on every compressor and lets an idle mixer rest. The channel strips run Multi-Comp 2's Opto, FET and VCA modes, the buses and the master its Bus mode, and the mastering stage its Multiband mode. Each COMP button on a strip, a bus or the master opens the plug-in's own editor, and the mastering page shows every multiband control in a panel of its own. A compressor that is engaged costs more CPU than the one it replaces, about three times as much at 48 kHz, because it always runs at the plug-in's own 2x oversampling. One that is out costs nothing. The channel EQ's frequency and Q knobs read and sound as they do on 4K EQ 2.

An idle mixer lets the CPU rest: Multicore DSP wakes only the threads a block needs, meters repaint only when what they show changes, several native panels draw far less often when idle, and a track with no plug-in on it that is muted or has no input costs the audio thread about a twentieth of what it did. On Linux the audio thread is now tested for locks and allocations with every change, and the PipeWire and ALSA audio threads no longer take a lock around each block.

MIDI is safer. Each recorded MIDI pass is written to the session folder as a Standard MIDI File, a pass in progress is saved as you play, at most once a second, and every save keeps a backup of the session. A session that cannot be opened offers its autosave and backups instead of failing. Clicking a key on the piano roll keyboard plays it.

SFZ and SF2 instruments that stayed silent after loading in 0.16.0 play again. A take recorded with PRINT on lands where a dry take of the same input does, where it used to land late by the channel's delay. LV2 plug-ins a Linux distribution installs in its lib64 folder appear in the plug-in picker, and the Linux download now needs the liblilv-0-0 and libserd-0-0 packages. A PipeWire graph that moves to a longer block no longer silences playback, a change of its rate is followed instead of going unnoticed, VST3 synths stop their notes at Stop, and sandboxed plug-ins run at audio priority where the system allows it. The built-in reverb, tape echo, tape machine and Sunset are their plug-ins' released versions, DuskVerb 2 1.0.2, Tape Echo 2 1.0.9, Tape Machine 2 1.0.13 and Sunset Circuits 1.1.0. Native panels show Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese and Korean names, and Hebrew and Arabic names read right to left.

Sessions save in format 12, which Dusk Studio 0.16.0 and earlier cannot open. Keep a copy before saving if you need to use an older version. An older session opens with its compressor settings converted to Multi-Comp 2's controls, so an older mix can sound different, and with each channel EQ band on the knob marking that plays where it played.

MIDI Merge layers performances into a region, with one undo step per loop pass while recording continues. The piano roll shows incoming notes live. Browse SFZ instruments from SFZ Instruments, Musical Artifacts, FreePats and Versilian Studios, see each pack's license, then download them to your installed library. Sessions keep the exact installed pack reference across computers. Playback readers share three fill workers and keep sample buffers near the playhead.
The mastering stage adds multiband phase analysis with held warnings, coherence and mono-loss readings. Its Mono monitor checks the fold-down while exports stay stereo.

Offline render quality can follow playback settings for faster bounces and freezes. Edits a plug-in reports trigger save prompts, failed state captures keep their last saved copy, and new unsaved sessions preserve earlier crash recovery and notes. Recording, export finalization and plug-in shutdown fixes protect sessions and generated audio.
Sessions save in format 11, which Dusk Studio 0.15.1 and earlier cannot open. Keep a copy before saving if you need to use an older version.
The piano roll follows the takes you record over its region, and playing the virtual keyboard during a take no longer changes the earlier take.
Every recording pass kept whole as a take, comping in the audio editor's take lanes, and the fixes from the 0.15 release review.

A built-in plugin suite that works on a fresh install (Utility, DuskVerb 2, Tape Echo 2, Tape Machine 2 and the Sunset synth), the 4K EQ 2 engine on the channels with EQ knobs that play the frequency they show, Tape Machine 2 on the master, a one-page quickstart, an offline instrument library, a first launch that picks an input and follows the system audio default, a signed checksum file, hardened session and plugin recovery, transport MIDI cleanup, and the fixes found by walking record, overdub and bounce on all three platforms and by testing each behaviour the manual documents.
Restores hosted plugin settings when reopening sessions, prevents hung plugin scans from wedging, and adds scan cancellation.

Fixes the macOS disk image, restores the notepad's full size on Retina Macs, protects Windows sessions from incompatible notepad graphics drivers and from unknown ones by refusing the notepad after a driver ends the application drawing it, removes Linux desktop files from macOS and Windows packages, and adds native CLAP and VST3 plugin hosting on Windows.

Adds the session notepad, a UI scale control, native PipeWire and macOS plugin hosting, MIDI hot-plug, loop take stacking, realtime hardware bounce, and a broad set of session, recording, audio-device, and plug-in fixes.
Manual recording latency offset with a sample readout for calibration; device restart and recording fixes.
Fixes the Windows build of 0.12.4.
Filterable program-grouped SoundFont preset browser.
Input monitoring now feeds aux sends during playback.
Beta patch: fixes a mixdown/stems/freeze crash with CLAP (and VST3/LV2) plugin inserts.
Beta patch: live play-along during playback, Mackie fader calibration, Windows plugin-scan sandbox fix, deterministic bounces.

Beta. Workflow: session sample-rate policy, seamless loop playback, Save As consolidation, aux return latency compensation, MIDI soft takeover, LV2 file state in sessions, delivery presets, and background audio imports. Sound: the console EQ on every channel and bus moves to a new-generation core with a subtle re-voicing, and the channel EQ and compressor path is lighter on the CPU. Launching on Wayland without XWayland now shows a clear message explaining how to enable it instead of crashing, and the MIDI engine internals have been modernised.

Patch release on the 0.11 Beta line. Chase / follow playhead in the timeline and editors, a bar / beat grid in the audio and MIDI editors, a reworked top-row layout with the stage selector in the menu row, and a keyboard-shortcut cleanup. Fixes a startup hang when the saved audio device is busy (falls back to another device with a notice) and an ALSA crash on interfaces with fewer than 32 channels. Adds a Raspberry Pi (arm64) Linux tarball.

Beta release. Optional out-of-process plugin sandbox with crash-isolated plugin scanning on all three OSes, automatic cross-track plugin delay compensation, broad undo coverage (notes, automation, tempo, renames), tempo editing from the ruler, portable session folders, MIDI Learn for EQ frequency/Q, multi-output cue routing, true-peak mastering limiter, and a data-integrity and real-time-safety hardening pass (atomic session save, autosave recovery, MIDI-out xruns, crash fixes on stop and quit).

First beta. MIDI binding targets across the mixer, screen-reader accessibility for the channel strips, audio-device hot-unplug recovery, macOS out-of-process plugin pipeline with in-process editors, and Linux arm64 builds.

Beta release leading up to 1.0. Phase 4 MIDI tempo retime, BPM-change confirmation dialog, 64-sample raised-cosine punch crossfade, triplet quantize variants, and packaging targets for Linux AppImage / deb / rpm, Windows MSI, macOS DMG.
